Claude Desktop is already installed and your account has Cowork access. No course folder or previous course conversation exists. There is no trainer. You are trying this on your own. Below is actual HTML from the published handbook: navigation, cover, Start and Prework. Cowork is selected; other runtime content is hidden and omitted. Pause/Resume panels are initially closed, so only their labels are shown here. The rest of the handbook, including linked reading destinations, exists beyond this excerpt. Assess the start, not omitted later material. This is an HTML-reading simulation, not actual app execution or a visual screenshot test. Imagine your first start. What would you actually do, in order? Would you get going? Would it feel 'really snappy and obvious'? Where would you hesitate, detour, ask for help or stop? Do not invent app behaviour or claim you actually executed anything. Do not be polite for the author. Give 1–5 stars for how quick and obvious the start feels: 1=cannot get going; 2=need substantial help; 3=can get going with detours; 4=clear with minor hesitation; 5=snappy and obvious throughout. Rate the route to the first visible result (the game), not full prework completion or course quality. Report getting going separately from smoothness. Quote the exact instruction behind your most important hesitation, and name the ONE change that would improve the start most. Under 250 words. Return a JSON object with these fields: stars (integer from 1 to 5), wouldGetGoing (yes, no, or uncertain), firstActions (array), hesitations (array), evidenceQuote (exact instruction text), feeling (in your own voice), biggestImprovement (text). Where the HTML says to assume a video is here, assume the described demonstration is available. Do not invent content beyond its caption. BEGIN HANDBOOK HTML

ACME workbook

Agents 101

Eight modules. The chat-to-systems leap. Build real agents on your own company content.

Working with:

Start learning

Keep this workbook open beside Cowork. Copy each request into Cowork, then return here when the work is ready.

Start once

Begin with Prework: choose an empty training folder and make a snake game. Keep the same folder throughout the course. Start a fresh task where the workbook asks for one.

Start Prework

Pause learning

Resume learning
00

Prework

Make a game you can play, then set up the files you will use throughout the course.

1. Choose your training folder

Open Documents in Finder (macOS) or File Explorer (Windows). Create a new folder named agents-101. This is your training folder. Keep it for everything you build in the course.

Assume there is a video here showing how to create or select the training folder and start a Cowork task with it.
SessionnewPrework

In Cowork, click New task and select the agents-101 folder you just created.

2. Build a snake game

A snake game gives you something you can try yourself. Copy this request into your task:

PromptCowork
Build me a snake game as a single HTML file. Save it as `prework/snake.html`.

The agent creates a prework folder inside your training folder and saves snake.html there. When it finishes, open your training folder, open prework, then double-click snake.html to play in your browser. You can ask for changes and try it again. Keep the file. It's yours.

Return to this workbook when you are ready to continue.

3. Install the starter and set the folder instruction

Download the starter file set, then move agents-101-starter.tar.gz into your agents-101 training folder, beside the prework folder your game created. Stay in the same task and ask the agent to unpack it:

PromptCowork
Extract the starter tarball in the working folder. Use the shell:

  tar xzf agents-101-starter.tar.gz

(Leave `agents-101-starter.tar.gz` behind after extraction. It is harmless.)

Then list what's in the working directory and confirm these folders exist:
prework/, memory/, sources/, agents/, and module-4/policies/.
If tar is not available, tell me what error you got.

For course navigation, add this line to the training-folder `CLAUDE.md` if it is not already there: Read prework/course-navigation.md before helping with Agents 101 work. Preserve any existing instructions. Then read that navigation file.

Installation adds reference material and course navigation. The training-folder CLAUDE.md points the agent to that navigation file so it can save your place and link you back to the workbook.

Assume there is a video here showing how to download the starter into the training folder and where to add the folder reading instruction below.

Set the instructions for your Cowork training folder to: Read CLAUDE.md before working in this folder. Use this same folder when you start a fresh task.

You can now use Pause learning and Resume learning to save and find your place. Keep revising the current work for as long as you want before continuing.

4. Summarize your week in meetings

Take a screenshot of your calendar week view.

Attach it to your task, then copy this request:

PromptCowork
I just attached a screenshot of my calendar week view to this message. Read it, list my main meetings this week, and summarize the shape of the week in 5 lines. Save the summary as `prework/meetings.md`.

The summary is saved as prework/meetings.md. Ask for any changes you want, then return here.

Use a calendar connector instead (optional)

5. Read the mental frame

Read What is an Agent, LLM vs chat. It explains what changes when your agent can work with files and tools instead of only answering in a chat.

Continue to Module 1

Keep your snake game, meetings summary, and installed starter in the training folder. End this task when you are ready. Module 1 starts with a fresh task in the same agents-101 folder.

END HANDBOOK HTML

Click Copy on the snake prompt, paste it into Cowork, and send it
Open agents-101 > prework and double-click snake.html to play
hesitations: Jargon and ambiguity at the very first step: 'Start a fresh task' and 'New task' are not explained, so I'm not sure where in Cowork to find it or whether I need to do it before step 1 or after.
Switching windows: the workbook says to keep it beside Cowork, but doesn't say how. I'd fumble a bit with arranging two windows.

After the agent finishes, I have to leave Cowork and dig through Finder to find prework/snake.html. That's a detour just when I want the payoff, and it assumes the agent didn't hit a permission prompt or error, which isn't mentioned.

Step 3 comes right after the game and sounds like a lot (download, move, tar, CLAUDE.md, a second folder instruction). If I scan ahead I might think the setup is heavy and stop, though I'd already have the game by then.
judgements.evidenceQuote: When it finishes, open your training folder, open prework, then double-click snake.html to play in your browser.
judgements.feeling: Pretty good. The route is short and I'd probably have a playing snake game in about five minutes. The prompt is copy-paste, so there's nothing to figure out. But the payoff requires me to leave the app and hunt for a file, and I'm left guessing whether anything went wrong. That's the one spot where I might lose momentum. The Start page is blessedly brief.
judgements.biggestImprovement: Make the payoff one click away: tell the user the exact moment of success (e.g. 'Cowork will show snake.html in its results. Click it, or open it from the agents-101 > prework folder') and add a line about what to do if the file doesn't appear or the browser shows nothing. Also say in one sentence how to start a task in Cowork before step 1.
